post_clip.description: A person approaches the storefront window, then repeatedly kicks or strikes the lower part of the glass panel (visible in frames 5–8), causing visible distortion and likely damage to the window frame/glass. This constitutes vandalism—damaging property where it stands—consistent with the defined anomaly type.

A person enters the frame at 22.5s and approaches the storefront window; by 28.5s, they are positioned directly in front of the glass, leaning slightly forward with hands near the lower part of the window—consistent with preparatory motion for vandalism (e.g., kicking or striking the window). No visible impact yet, but posture and proximity to vulnerable property (large glass panels) in a deserted setting raise high suspicion of imminent property damage.

The person repeatedly kicks or strikes the lower part of the store's glass window frame or door with their right foot (visible in frames 6–12), consistent with vandalism—damaging property where it stands. No entry attempt is observed; the action is focused on impacting the fixed structure.
